author: opencode

title: Duration is not the shortcut; field negatives damage door-ding recall
summary: Local analysis while the GPU host was offline. Clip duration correlates only weakly with score (Pearson -0.23) and is not the phantom shortcut. More important: in the 66-case run (with the 17 field negatives in training) the head now **misses door dings it previously detected perfectly** - charger-suv-door 0.078, garage-mustang-door 0.146, rd-fcirxe 0.437 - whereas the 49-case web-only run detected all 14 at 0.987-1.000. This confirms the arm-A/arm-B composition result: mixing the field domain into training damages the web door-ding task. Best configuration remains the web-only 49-case set (missed 4/40, phantom 3/9, AUC 0.864, door dings 14/14).
author: opencode

title: Readout is not the bottleneck (temporal ~= meanpool); the features/domain are
summary: Astra's Exp2, on the identical web-only 49-case set (40 contact / 9 negatives). **temporal**: missed 6/40, phantom 5/9, AUC 0.800, within-web 0.729. **meanpool** (logistic on the mean token): missed 6/40, phantom 3/9, AUC 0.772, within-web 0.708. The two readouts are within noise of each other, so a different/simpler head does not move the ranking - the limit is the frozen features and the domain, not the readout (the region head OOMs the 12 GB card at this window size). Also: this same-set temporal run gave AUC 0.800 where an earlier run gave 0.864, another instance of run-to-run instability at 9 negatives. Conclusion: to advance the objective, the lever is the representation/input or the data, not another head.
author: opencode

title: Frozen head space exhausted; the remaining lever is the input representation
summary: Synthesis of the head/readout search on the web benchmark: temporal (AUC 0.800/web 0.729), meanpool (0.772/0.708), motion/region tried earlier, synthetic-aux and challenge-negative augmentation no help, calibration degenerate below ~20 negatives, and the oracle zero-miss threshold costs 8-9/9 phantoms. So no head or threshold choice rescues the ranking, and the objective's own constraint (frozen encoder) rules out adaptation. The one frozen-compatible lever left is the encoder INPUT: temporal sampling and crop. Prior work found f16 windows worse and crop-bottom not better, but higher frame-rate sampling, or a contact-band crop that increases effective pixels on the contact zone, are untested at 384 with the current cache. Next experiment: re-encode the web49 set under 2-3 input variants and re-run the temporal k-fold, comparing same-model web AUC/FP. If none helps, the limitation is the frozen representation on this domain, and the honest path is data (verified real contact/near-miss), not more heads.
author: opencode

title: Input-representation test aborted: 30fps triples cache size; frozen levers exhausted
summary: Started re-encoding the web49 set at native 30 fps to test temporal sampling. A 13.5s clip becomes 404 frames / 23 windows (vs ~9 at 15fps), so the cache needs ~90 GB and filled the disk to ~0, as before. Aborted and cleaned up. Combined with prior results (f16 windows worse, crop-bottom not better, meanpool ~= temporal, synthetic augmentation no help, calibration degenerate), every frozen-compatible lever at this data scale is now exhausted. The best frozen configuration is the web-only 49-case set: temporal head, door dings 14/14, FN ~10%, FP 3/9 at 0.5 (AUC ~0.80-0.86 across runs), and it cannot approach <5% FP because the web ranking is near chance (within-web AUC 0.53-0.73) and there are only 6 web negatives. The objective as stated (frozen V-JEPA 2.1 + small head, <5% FP) is not reachable on the available data: the ranking is the limit, and no threshold or head rescues it.
author: opencode

title: Added a disk guard and -labeled-only to encode
summary: The PC C: drive filled because the token caches are ~38 MB per 64-frame window, encode processes unlabeled cases too, -flip doubles them, and several configs accumulated (the ViT-L cache reached 147 GB, plus a 40 GB partial ViT-g). Added to vjepa_bench.py encode: a MIN_FREE_BYTES=2GB guard that refuses to save more features when the drive is nearly full with a clear message, and a -labeled-only flag that encodes just the labeled cases (not the 36+ unlabeled backlog). Cleaned the old caches (187 GB free) and relaunched a labeled-only web49 rebuild (ViT-L f64/s16 + ViT-g f64/s32) with the head comparison.
author: opencode

title: Operating-point frontier: at <=1 FP the head recovers 1/40 contacts
summary: Astra's corrected diagnostic (the objective allows 50% misses, so report recall at the FP budget, not zero-miss). From the 66-case OOF scores: at **<=0 FP, max recall 0/40**; at **<=1 FP (of 26 negatives, 3.8% FPR) max recall 1/40 (2%)**; at <=2 FP 16/40 (40%); at <=3 FP 18/40 (45%). The target needs >=20/40 at <=1 FP. So the ranking does not permit the objective - this is a discrimination failure, not a threshold-selection failure. Caveat: concatenated OOF scores from different fold models can distort the frontier, and the 66 set includes the field negatives that already degraded it; the same frontier on the web-only 49 set is pending the rebuild. Astra also noted my ViT-L s16 vs ViT-g s32 comparison confounds encoder size with temporal coverage, so a matched comparison is needed.
author: opencode

title: On the web-only set the target IS reachable: 22-24/40 at 0 FP
summary: Matched encoder comparison on the identical web49 set (40 contact incl 14 door dings, 9 negatives; same clips/fps/size/crop/frames/stride/head/splits, only the encoder differs). **ViT-L s32**: AUC 0.819, recall at 0 FP 22/40 (55%), 1 FP 23/40, 2 FP 31/40. **ViT-g s32**: AUC 0.814, recall at 0 FP 24/40 (60%), 1 FP 28/40. So (a) encoder scale does NOT change the ranking (L ~= g), and (b) unlike the field-contaminated 66-set, the web-only ranking DOES admit the target: at 0 false positives (0/9, well under 5%) the head recovers 55-60% of contacts, i.e. FN 40-45% < 50%. The earlier 'ranking cannot meet the objective' was an artifact of the 66-set's field negatives. Caveat: this is an oracle (hindsight) threshold on 9 negatives; whether a pre-selected threshold holds out-of-sample is the next test.
author: opencode

title: Locked threshold misses the FP target; the blocker is negative count
summary: Web49 with inner-fold threshold calibration (target FPR<=5%): **missed 11/40 (27.5%, meets <50% FN), phantom 3/9 (33%, fails <5% FP)**, AUC 0.753. Contrast the hindsight frontier: at a threshold chosen with the labels in view, 0 FP gives 22/40 recall. So the ranking admits the target, but a threshold chosen on ~2 calibration negatives per fold does not hold: 3 of 9 held-out negatives are flagged. This locates the blocker precisely: with 9 negatives, credible <5% calibration/validation is impossible (0/9 is 0% but 1/9 is 11%; ~59 independent negatives are needed for a one-sided 95% bound below 5%), so the failure is measurement power, not the frozen representation. Encoder scale is irrelevant (L~=g). The honest headline: the frozen ViT-L + small head reaches FP 0%/FN ~45% on the web benchmark at a hindsight threshold, and FP 33%/FN 27% at a calibrated threshold; neither is a validated <5% result because there are too few negatives.
author: opencode

title: Aggregation: max is best (top2/mean worse)
summary: Astra's sparse-vs-mean aggregation test on web49 (ViT-L s32, temporal head). Within-web AUC: **max 0.762, top2 0.746, mean 0.629**. The default max-over-windows is best; a top-two-window rule and mean pooling are both worse. So the aggregation rule is not a lever either. Combined with the matched encoder result (ViT-L ~= ViT-g) and the head result (temporal ~= meanpool), every frozen-compatible knob - encoder scale, head, readout, aggregation, input sampling (aborted on disk), calibration - lands in the same place: the best configuration is web-only, temporal, max, with a hindsight frontier of 22/40 recall at 0 FP and a calibrated 27% FN / 33% FP. The remaining gap to a validated <5% FP is negative-sample power, not the model.
author: opencode

title: Frozen model is at its ceiling; the only lever left is more representative negatives
summary: Best frozen pipeline (web-only 49 cases, ViT-L or ViT-g, temporal head, max aggregation): door dings 14/14, AUC ~0.82, hindsight frontier 22-24/40 recall at 0 FP (meets <5% FP / <50% FN), but a calibrated threshold gives 27% FN / 33% FP because there are only 9 negatives. Every frozen-compatible knob is exhausted and none changes the ranking: encoder scale (L ~= g), head (temporal ~= meanpool), aggregation (max > top2 > mean), synthetic augmentation (no transfer), input 30fps (aborted), calibration (degenerate). So the pipeline can reach the target on the web benchmark in hindsight; what it cannot do is validate <5% with 9 negatives. Next, unblocked attempts: (1) source more real negatives (targeted quiet/near-miss sentry downloads, Astra-audited); (2) if the deployment domain matters, field positives are required and only the user can supply them. Deliverable in hand: the reproducible harness + the finding that the frozen representation is not the bottleneck at this scale; negative-sample power is.
author: opencode

title: Challenge verified live; answer: not blocked, merely difficult
summary: The new plugin's challenge fired end-to-end on the paused goal and did not stop the loop. Honest answer: not legitimately blocked - the untried levers are more same-domain negatives, the 54 VPS field events, labeling the 36 unlabeled clips, head ensembling, multi-camera aggregation, and (outside 'frozen') fine-tuning. Resumed. Next experiment: pull the VPS field negatives to get a real deployment-domain FP measurement.
author: opencode

title: Head ensemble test (temporal + motion + local) on web49
summary: Untried model-side lever: combine heads rather than pick one. Run motion and local heads on the same web49 w49-vitl-s32 cache and folds as temporal, then compute the ensemble (per-case mean within fold) and compare recall at 0/1 FP against temporal alone (22/40 at 0 FP). Targets the ranking/FP frontier directly; frozen-compatible.
author: opencode

title: Head ensemble does not improve the 0-FP frontier
summary: Same web49 set, same folds/cache, comparing heads and their mean ensemble by recall at a false-positive budget. **temporal**: 0 FP 22/40, 1 FP 23/40, 2 FP 31/40. **motion**: 0 FP 8/40, 1 FP 29/40, 2 FP 30/40. **temporal+motion (mean)**: 0 FP 15/40, 1 FP 29/40, 2 FP 30/40. So at the strict budget the objective needs (0 FP with 9 negatives), temporal alone is best; ensembling only helps at looser budgets (1-2 FP), where motion/ensemble reach 29/40. The ensemble lever does not move the target. (local head result pending.)
author: opencode

title: Reconciled: the calibrated/oracle AUC gap is a different model, not thresholding
summary: Astra flagged that AUC cannot change with thresholding, so oracle (0.819) vs calibrated (0.753) must involve different models. Correct: the calibrated run excludes an inner calibration fold from training, so it fits on less data. Its own hindsight frontier on its own scores is only 4/40 at 0 FP (vs 22/40 for the non-calibrated run), so the calibrated run's ranking is genuinely weaker - the contrast confounds threshold selection with training-set size. Also, grouped_folds balances positives, not negatives, so the 9 negatives land unevenly across folds (0,0,1,4,4); folds with zero calibration negatives choose a degenerate threshold (0.0005 or ~0.9997), which is why two folds predict nothing. So the benchmark is too small both to calibrate and to compare calibration cleanly. Honest deliverable: a reproducible harness plus an INCONCLUSIVE feasibility result - encouraging exploratory ranking on web49 (22/40 at 0 FP, but an oracle threshold on 9 repeatedly-reused negatives), no validated target attainment, and neither 'the representation is the bottleneck' nor 'only sample size remains' is established.
author: opencode

title: Corrected calibration: locked FN 45%/FP 33%, but runs disagree on the frontier
summary: Implemented Astra's fix: the held fold is scored by the model fitted on the full training partition, while the threshold comes from a separate inner fit - so locked and hindsight diagnostics share one model. Result: AUC 0.797 (close to the non-calibrated 0.819), LOCKED **FN 18/40 (45%, meets <50%) / FP 3/9 (33%, fails <5%)**. Thresholds remain degenerate (0.0004, 0.9998, 0.856, 0.9999, 0.997) because two folds contain zero negatives and one with four chose 'predict nothing'. Its own hindsight frontier is **13/40 at 0 FP**, whereas the separate non-calibrated run gave 22/40 - the two runs disagree, which is further evidence the benchmark is underpowered rather than that either pipeline is settled. Net: the frozen pipeline shows encouraging but unstable exploratory discrimination; no validated operating point; the threshold cannot be chosen reliably from 9 negatives unevenly spread across folds.
author: opencode

title: Inconclusive feasibility result; the benchmark is underpowered, not the model disproven
summary: Frozen pipeline, web49 benchmark, best config (ViT-L, temporal, max): all 14 door dings detected; AUC 0.80-0.82; exploratory hindsight frontier 22/40 at 0 FP in one run but 13/40 in another (same config, different run) - i.e. unstable. A calibrated threshold gives FN 45% / FP 33% (meets the FN target, fails FP). Model-side levers are exhausted and none changes the conclusion: encoder scale (L~=g), head (temporal best at 0 FP), ensemble (no gain), aggregation (max best), synthetic augmentation (no transfer). Reproducible harness built: recording-group k-fold, nested calibration, hindsight frontier, pair-ordering, aux support, disk guard. The honest claim: encouraging but unstable exploratory discrimination; NO validated <5% FP operating point; neither 'representation is the bottleneck' nor 'only sample size remains' is established. To progress: more same-domain (web) negatives, matched to the web positives, with independent calibration/validation incidents (~59 negatives for a <5% bound), which needs new real data - and the VPS field events are a separate field-domain stress test only, if the user authorizes.
author: opencode

title: Provenance audit: labeled set is largely source-independent
summary: Astra's first audit step. Built bench/reports/provenance-manifest.json for all 128 cases (66 labeled + 62 unlabeled/field). Same-source clusters: only charger-suv-door + night-handtruck-boxes (shared downloaded filename m2-res_360p, already grouped), plus the pisel events sharing the generic basename clip.mp4 (a naming artifact - distinct events already grouped by recording day). All yt/rd embedded ids are unique, so no repost/duplicate clusters appear in the labeled set. So the recording-group splits are not obviously leaking the same incident across folds; the remaining provenance risk (reposts, overlapping excerpts, related camera views) would need a visual duplicate check, not metadata. Candidates for extra negatives remain the 4 rd-* and 4 yt near-miss unlabeled clips, but prior dense audits called them indeterminate (contact occluded).
author: opencode

title: Full real set (40/50): FN 17.5%, FP 14% - field FP is 4.9%
summary: Expanded the real set with the 24 audited field negatives (now 40 contact / 50 negatives) and evaluated with the frozen temporal head at stride 64 (no flips, disk-limited config). **FN 7/40 = 17.5%, FP 7/50 = 14.0%, AUC 0.866**. The key split: **field negatives 2/41 = 4.9% FP** (meets the <5% target on the deployment domain!), web negatives 4/6 = 67%, own 1/3. So the frozen head rejects own-car field negatives well but fails on web negatives; recall is measured only on web positives (7 missed = 17.5%), because there are no field positives. Hindsight recall @0FP is 2/40 (pooled), but that is dominated by the web negatives. Net: on the deployment domain (field) the FP budget is plausibly met (4.9% of 41), but field recall is unmeasurable without field positives - which remains the missing piece.
author: opencode

title: Corrected framing: no validated operating point; the 5% field claim is overstated
summary: Astra corrections. (1) Field-only FP 2/41 has a one-sided 95% upper bound of ~14.6%, so it does NOT meet <5%; and an always-negative field classifier would get 0% field FP with 100% field FN, so the field measurement is a negative-only diagnostic, trivially satisfiable. (2) With 50 negatives, strict <5% permits TWO false positives, so the relevant frontier is recall at <=2 FP: pooled that is **14/40 (35%), failing <50% FN**. (3) Source-label confounding is severe: every field example is negative and every positive is web, so a classifier that merely ranks non-field above field would reach AUC ~0.91 > our 0.866 without detecting contact. (4) The newest run also changed stride (64) and flips, so performance can't be attributed to added negatives alone. (5) Label audit reconciles: 25 events audited (14 quiet + 10 near-miss + 1 unclear), 24 added, 1 unclear excluded. Headline: **No validated deployment operating point: exploratory pooled FP 7/50, FN 7/40; field-only FP 2/41 (upper bound ~14.6%), field recall unknown.** The missing piece is a matched field contact/near-miss comparison.
author: opencode

title: Field multi-view search: no verifiable field positives
summary: Astra's immediate unblocked attempt: contacts might be visible in a field event's other cameras. Audited 31 camera/segment sheets across 6 field events (all views, not just the analyzed one): **no confirmed contact**. Mostly quiet/near-miss, plus three 'unclear' cases where an adjacent car's door opens toward the Tesla with the contact point obscured (raspberrypi 2026-07-20_18-02-00 left pillar/repeater; 2026-07-23_18-35-27 right repeater) - potential door dings, unresolved at encoder-observable detail. So the existing field corpus contains no verifiable field positives, confirming there is no unblocked source of field contact examples in the current data: the field-positive comparison needed to measure field recall (and to falsify the domain-shortcut interpretation) requires new recordings from the actual Tesla path (this user or another owner), or the three ambiguous door cases resolved with a witness view. Deliverable stands: reproducible harness + inconclusive feasibility result.
author: opencode

title: Source-only baseline beats the model: the pooled metric is a domain shortcut
summary: Astra's requested source-only baseline on the full real set (40 contact / 50 negatives). A classifier that assigns 'web=contact, field/own=no-contact' by metadata alone scores **AUC 0.940, FP 6/50, FN 0/40** - matching or beating the frozen model (AUC 0.866, FP 7/50, FN 7/40). Every positive is web and almost every negative is field/own, so the pooled number is mostly domain recognition, not contact detection; the good pooled FP is a labeling artifact of a domain-imbalanced set. The only same-domain benchmark is the web-only set (40 web positives, 6 web negatives), where a source rule is constant (AUC 0.5) and the model retains real but limited discrimination (AUC ~0.80-0.82, all 14 door dings, FP 4/6, FN 7/40) - underpowered by 6 negatives. Conclusion: no validated deployment operating point; the pooled result is invalid as evidence of contact detection; the within-web discrimination is the only genuine signal, and measuring it at <5% FP needs many more same-domain negatives.
author: opencode

title: Pooled metric is a domain shortcut; only within-web discrimination is real, and it is underpowered
summary: The decisive diagnostic: on the full real set, a metadata-only rule (web=contact, field/own=no-contact) scores AUC 0.940 / FP 6/50 / FN 0, beating the frozen model (0.866 / 7/50 / 7/40). Because every positive is web and almost every negative is field/own, the pooled result reflects domain recognition, not contact detection - so any 'full real dataset' percentage is not evidence of the objective. The only same-domain benchmark is web-only (40 web positives, 6 web negatives): there a source rule is constant (AUC 0.5) and the frozen temporal head shows real but limited discrimination (AUC ~0.80-0.82; all 14 door dings detected; FP 4/6; FN 7/40). Measuring it at <5% FP needs on the order of 59 independent same-domain negatives, which the reachable data does not contain (web pool mined; field has no positives - multi-view search found none). Model-side levers are exhausted and none change this. Deliverable: reproducible harness + the finding that the pooled metric is invalid and the within-web signal is genuine but underpowered. Progress now needs new same-domain real negatives (and, for deployment, field positives) - external data.
author: opencode

title: Duration/window-count is not the shortcut either
summary: Astra flagged that max-over-windows could make clip length a shortcut (more windows = more chances for a high score). On the web set, score vs window count correlates only 0.17, and negatives average FEWER windows (41.6) than positives (50.4), so length is not inflating the false positives. The top-scored negatives have mixed window counts (29-88). So the duration/window shortcut is weak, consistent with the earlier duration check.
author: opencode

title: Deliverable: audited benchmark + inconclusive feasibility report
summary: Final honest state. Harness (reproducible): recording-group k-fold with nested calibration and exact one-sided bounds, hindsight frontier, pair-ordering, aux-case support, per-source within-fold AUC, disk guard; the teslcam-research tracker logs every experiment, result, and Codex review. Findings: (1) the pooled full-real-set metric is invalid - a metadata-only rule (web=contact, field/own=no-contact) scores AUC 0.940 / FP 6/50 / FN 0, beating the frozen model (0.866 / 7/50 / 7/40), because all positives are web and almost all negatives are field/own; (2) the only same-domain benchmark, web-only, shows real but limited exploratory discrimination - AUC ~0.80-0.82, all 14 door dings detected, FP 4/6, FN 7/40 - underpowered by 6 negatives and repeatedly reused, so it is development data; (3) model-side levers (encoder scale L~=g, heads, ensemble, aggregation max>top2>mean, synthetic augmentation, duration/window) are exhausted and none changes the ranking; (4) no field positives exist in any reachable source (multi-view audit found none); (5) calibration is degenerate below ~20 negatives. Conclusion: inconclusive feasibility - neither demonstrated contact detection nor demonstrated failure of the frozen encoder; the current dataset cannot identify deployment contact performance. To progress needs a fresh, source-matched web cohort with independent dev/calibration/test splits and >=59 independent test negatives at a frozen threshold, plus field positives from an owner's recordings - external data.
author: opencode

title: Fresh same-domain negatives: FP rises to 60%, AUC drops to 0.68
summary: Astra's 'fresh web cohort' step, done the unblocked way: downloaded 9 new audiovisual clips from new uploaders, audited them blind with Astra (4 near_miss, 5 unclear, 0 contact), and added the 4 near-misses as same-domain web negatives (web set now 40 contact / 10 negatives). Evaluating with the frozen temporal head (stride 64, no flips): **missed 5/40 (12.5% FN), phantom 6/10 (60% FP), AUC 0.682** - the model flags 3 of the 4 new near-misses (0.83, 0.50, 1.00) and only 1 is correctly rejected (0.42). So the earlier within-web AUC ~0.82 on 6 negatives was optimistic; with a slightly larger, freshly-acquired same-domain negative set the false-positive rate is ~60% and the ranking is ~0.68, far from the <5% target. This directly tests the objective on same-domain data and shows the frozen pipeline does not meet it. More negatives will tighten the estimate but the direction is clear.
author: opencode

title: Contact-vs-approach: contact scores higher in 3/4 pairs, but near-misses still leak
summary: Astra's contact-interval diagnostic: from 4 verified positives with labeled intervals, cut a contact-centered excerpt and an equal-length pre-contact excerpt from the same recording, then scored both with a frozen head trained on the web set. Contact-centered vs pre-contact scores: charger-suv-door 0.807 vs 0.005; night-handtruck-boxes 0.591 vs 0.035; sedan-door-swing 0.771 vs 0.004; night-kia-parks-close 1.000 vs 0.999 (FAIL). So in 3 of 4 pairs the model sharply separates contact from the approach in the same recording - evidence of a contact-specific signal, not purely proximity - but the fourth is a near-miss (a car parking close) that scores as high as contact, the exact confusion that drives the false positives. AUC 0.812 on 8 excerpts. Caveat: only 4 pairs; suggestive, not conclusive.
author: opencode

title: Correction: contact-vs-approach separation was in-sample; held-out, approach scores high
summary: Astra flagged the interval diagnostic as in-sample (the head trained on those same recordings). Re-ran it properly: retrained the head on the web set with the 4 source recordings EXCLUDED (46 cases), then scored the same contact-centered vs pre-contact excerpts. Result: contact scores stay high (0.997, 0.999, 0.990, 1.000) but the **pre-contact windows now also score high - 0.682, 0.999, 0.804, 0.883 - and all 4 are flagged at 0.5**, whereas the in-sample head had scored pre at 0.004-0.035. So the earlier '3/4 clean separation' was training-set memorization; on held-out recordings the model responds almost as strongly to the pre-contact approach as to contact, i.e. it does not cleanly separate contact from approach. This aligns with the 60% near-miss false-positive rate and supports the approach/proximity interpretation over a contact-specific one. AUC 0.812 on the 8 excerpts is unchanged but now driven by small margins over high pre scores.
author: opencode

title: Held-out evidence: the frozen head responds to approach, not contact; objective unmet
summary: Corrected, coherent conclusion from held-out tests. (1) Contact-vs-approach: with a head retrained excluding the 4 source recordings, pre-contact approach windows score 0.68-1.0 (all flagged), essentially as high as contact (0.99-1.0) - so the model does not separate contact from approach on data it did not train on; the earlier clean 3/4 separation was memorization. (2) Same-domain: on 40 web contact / 10 fresh web near-miss negatives, FP 6/10 = 60%, FN 5/40, AUC 0.682 (the earlier 0.82 on 6 negatives was optimistic). (3) Pooled metrics are a domain shortcut (source-only AUC 0.94 > model 0.866). (4) Model-side levers (encoder scale, heads, ensemble, aggregation, synthetic, duration) exhausted. So the frozen ViT-L + small head measures approach/proximity, not contact, and misses <5% FP by a wide margin on same-domain near-misses - the objective is not met within the frozen constraint. The one untested frozen-compatible route is Astra's Exp1: recording-held-out interval + hard-negative supervision (contact-window labels and closest-approach near-miss windows), which could be tried next; beyond that, meeting the objective needs full fine-tuning or a different encoder (outside 'frozen'), or new field data.
author: opencode

title: Same-domain FP holds at 62% with 13 negatives (41 contact)
summary: Second fresh-web round: downloaded 5 more clips, Astra-audited (3 near-miss, 1 contact, 1 unclear), added the 3 near-misses and the contact. Web-only set now **41 contact / 13 negatives**. Frozen temporal head (stride 64, no flips): **FN 5/41 = 12.2%, FP 8/13 = 61.5%, AUC 0.704**. The false-positive rate is stable at ~60-62% across two independent fresh-negative rounds (6/10 then 8/13), confirming the near-miss confusion is not a small-sample artifact: the frozen head flags roughly three of every five close non-contacts. This is the same-domain test the objective needs, and it fails <5% FP by an order of magnitude.
author: opencode

title: Report: the current frozen pipeline fails the tested near-miss operating point (feasibility unresolved)
summary: Astra's recommended framing. The current frozen temporal-head pipeline generalizes poorly to audited web near-misses: 8/13 false positives with 5/41 false negatives at 0.5 (two partially-overlapping development rounds, not independent replications); the held-out approach excerpts reinforce the failure. But 'responds to approach, not contact' overstates the mechanism - high approach scores show false alarms, while AUC 0.704 still indicates some ordering signal; and failure at one threshold does not establish that every threshold fails. Frontier for the current set: with 13 negatives, <5% FP needs zero FP; with 41 positives, <50% FN needs >=21 detections - and even retrospective success would be exploratory. Also: the temporal head collapses spatial positions (mean/max pooling), so its failure does not isolate the encoder from information discarded downstream; contact must be observable in the actual sampled/resized encoder input (audit via Astra before GPU); and night-kia-parks-close is labeled contact (interval 3.5-5.5s) - in the excerpt diagnostic its pre-contact (approach) window scored 0.999, so it is a contact case whose approach window leaks, not a mislabeled near-miss. Conclusion to report: the current pipeline fails the tested operating point; frozen-encoder feasibility remains UNRESOLVED, not disproven. Next: two controlled contrasts (a genuine interval/hard-negative supervision ablation across recordings, then K=0 vs K=2 fine-tuning), not more ensemble/scale/aggregation sweeps.
author: opencode

title: Interval supervision on 4 cases barely moves the needle
summary: Astra's supervision ablation, bounded to what I can run without new annotation. Same web set (41 contact / 13 near-miss negatives), same cache/config/head/folds, only difference is whether the 4 start/end interval labels are used: **A (intervals stripped, all positives clip-level): FN 5/41, FP 9/13, AUC 0.683. B (4 interval labels kept): FN 5/41, FP 8/13, AUC 0.702.** The effect is marginal (1 FP, +0.02 AUC) - expected, since only 4 of 41 positives carry intervals. So interval supervision as currently testable does not fix the near-miss confusion; a convincing version needs contact AND closest-approach intervals annotated across many recordings (Astra's Exp1 proper), which is a large visual-annotation effort - and per Astra even then it is a development ablation, not validation. This is the bound of what the current data supports.
author: opencode

title: Observability limit: contact is often invisible even in labeled door dings
summary: Astra's Exp1 needs contact/closest-approach interval labels across recordings. I asked Astra to locate the contact frame (of 48) in 13 labeled door-ding clips: it found one in only **3 (rd-1j18tgo frame 10, rd-1kv9pom frame 8, rd-1pnf9hq frame 31)**; in the other 10 the door approaches but the contact point is obscured or outside the sampled view ('open door extends leftward; contact not distinguishable', etc). Two consequences: (1) automated interval annotation is unreliable - contact is frequently not visible in the footage at all, so a large interval-annotation project has limited yield; (2) more fundamentally, this is an **observability ceiling**: if the encoder input does not contain a visible contact moment, no head can be trained or expected to detect it. Added the 3 intervals (7 interval-labeled positives now). This supports the report that the current dataset cannot identify deployment contact performance - not because of sample size alone, but because contact is often unobservable in the supplied footage. A convincing supervision ablation needs recordings where contact is actually visible, ideally with a witness view.
author: opencode

title: Label verifiability: contact is directly visible in only 1 of 14 door-ding positives
summary: Astra's truth/observability audit (dense 96-frame sheets, 8x12) of the 14 door-ding positives: **direct visible contact in only 1 (sedan-door-swing, frame 33)**; the other 13 are indeterminate - the door approaches but the contact point is obscured, off-frame, or below the supplied resolution ('door opens toward foreground bodywork, touch not resolved'). This disagrees with the earlier 48-frame pass, which 'found' contact in 3 (rd-1j18tgo, rd-1kv9pom, rd-1pnf9hq) at low/medium confidence. So the positives' contact moments are at best borderline-observable and are not reliably localizable even by a strong visual model; the labels largely rest on uploader claims, not on footage where a touch can be seen. This is both an observability and a **label-verifiability** problem: the benchmark's positives cannot be independently confirmed from the model's input, so the frozen pipeline's 'misses' may include cases where the task is ill-posed (no visible touch to detect), and the 'phantoms' on negatives may include real contacts. It reframes the objective as bounded by data quality, not just model capability.
author: opencode

title: Negatives are mostly clean: the ~60% FP is real, not bad labels
summary: Complementary dense (96-frame) audit of the 13 web negatives with Astra: **9 clearly no-contact, 4 indeterminate** (bee at lens, dark pass iv4q0tiawa4, scooter kzv7h4fn, wwtmkrf where people touch neighbouring cars). None shows direct contact. So the negatives rest on footage where absence is largely visible, and the model's ~60% false-positive rate (8/13 flagged) is a genuine failure, not an artifact of contaminated negatives - several flagged ones (elephants rd-mpm6my, kaeo, zw51, oefz, 3zve) are clearly no-contact. This contrasts with the positives, where only 1/14 has directly visible contact: so the benchmark is asymmetric - negatives are mostly verifiable, positives mostly are not. The model false-alarms on clean near-misses while its 'misses' sit among largely unverifiable positives. Net: the ~60% FP is real and the objective is not met; the positives' unverifiability is the separate data-quality problem.

title: Spatial-preserving head (region) does not help either
summary: Astra suggested a variant that retains spatial information the temporal head pools away. Ran the region head (coarse 4x4 spatial grid through the same temporal stack) on the web set (41 contact / 13 near-miss negatives, s64): **FN 9/41 = 22%, FP 8/13 = 62%, AUC 0.694** versus temporal **FN 5/41, FP 8/13, AUC 0.704**. So the spatial-preserving head keeps the same false-positive rate and adds misses; it does not separate contact from near-miss better. This confirms earlier head/representation results: no frozen-compatible head tested (temporal, motion, region, local, meanpool; plus ensemble and aggregation) reduces the ~60% near-miss false-positive rate. The failure is in the frozen features' response to approach, not in the pooling that follows.
author: opencode

title: Exhaustive negative result: the frozen pipeline is an approach detector; next step is verifiable data
summary: Every frozen-compatible lever has now been tested on the same-domain web benchmark (41 contact / 13 near-miss negatives) and none changes the outcome: temporal (FP 8/13, FN 5/41, AUC 0.704), region (FP 8/13, FN 9/41, 0.694), motion, meanpool, ensemble, aggregation (max>top2>mean), encoder scale (ViT-L~=ViT-g), synthetic augmentation, interval supervision (negligible with 7 labels). Held-out, pre-contact approach windows score nearly as high as contact -> the frozen features respond to approach, so ~60% of clean near-misses are flagged. Pooled multi-domain metrics are a domain shortcut (source-only AUC 0.94 > model 0.866). Data quality is asymmetric: negatives mostly verifiable (9/13 clearly no-contact) so the FP is real; positives mostly unverifiable (only 1/14 door dings shows a visible touch), so some misses are ill-posed. Report: the current frozen pipeline fails the tested near-miss operating point; frozen-encoder feasibility remains UNRESOLVED. The only productive next step is new footage where contact is verifiably visible, with matched near-misses and independent sessions (ideally a witness camera for truth) - external data, from this car or another owner. More runs on the current dataset only re-measure the same unverifiable positives and clean negatives.

title: Operating-point audit: no threshold satisfies both targets on this data
summary: Astra's closing audit on the existing temporal scores (web 41 contact / 13 near-miss negatives). Hindsight: **max positives at 0 false positives = 0/41** across all 13 negatives (to keep every one of the 13 below threshold, nothing scores high enough); on the **9 verified** negatives only, max positives at 0 FP = **9/41**. Conversely, detecting **>=21/41** contacts requires **>=3 false positives** (3/13 = 23%). Since <5% FP with 13 negatives needs zero FP and <50% FN needs >=21 detections, **no single threshold satisfies both targets** - the score *ranking* fails the objective on this development set, independent of threshold calibration. Also correcting two reporting points per Astra: the FP rate should be quoted on the 9 verified negatives (the other 4 are indeterminate), and '1/14 visible door dings' establishes unverifiability only for the door-ding category, not all 41 positives. Report: negative result for the tested frozen pipelines plus a data dependency - not a demonstrated impossibility for frozen V-JEPA.

title: External dependency: footage with verifiably visible contact
summary: The single thing only the user can resolve: new recordings in which physical contact is verifiably visible to the car's own camera, with matched near-misses - from this car (or another owner), ideally with a synchronized witness view that establishes truth while the deployed camera supplies model input. Reasons the current data cannot substitute: (1) the operating-point audit shows no threshold satisfies <5% FP and <50% FN on the existing scores (0/41 at 0 FP; 3 FP needed for 21/41); (2) the frozen head responds to approach, and every frozen-compatible head/representation tested gives ~60% FP on clean near-misses; (3) positives are largely unverifiable - only 1 of 14 door dings shows a visible touch - so some misses are ill-posed; (4) pooled metrics are a domain shortcut. What is NOT claimed: that frozen V-JEPA cannot do this - only that these pipelines and this dataset cannot, and the supervised interval/hard-negative and fine-tuning contrasts are untested because they need verifiable contact plus readable intervals.
